topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Biology and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture opens with a welcome, course structure details, and an outline of the learning objectives.

topics.label: Cellular and Architectural Breakdown in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops from accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal developmental differentiation and three-dimensional tissue architecture.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion and Metastatic Spread
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the clinical and histological distinctions between benign and malignant tumors based on local tissue invasion and metastatic dissemination.

topics.label: Neoplastic Progression and Tumor Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how neoplasms progress from benign precursor states to malignant disease and define the standard conventions used to classify and name them.

topics.label: Pathophysiology, Mortality, and Comparative Incidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms by which tumors cause illness and death while comparing patterns of cancer incidence across human organs and diverse animal species.

topics.label: Clinical Detection and Cancer Screening Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the rationale, diagnostic methods, and clinical efficacy of screening programs designed to detect pre-malignant and early-stage cancers.

topics.label: Conclusion and Practical Preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture closes with a recap of the learning outcomes and administrative signposting for upcoming practical sessions.
